topic: Proportional-dimensional HIR regret phase transition in a binary randomized trial. Let p/n tend to kappa in a compact subset of (0,1/2), q be standard Gaussian in R^p, A be Bernoulli(1/2), and Y be binary with arm-invariant mean expit(gamma q_1), gamma bounded away from zero. Compare maximizers over ||theta||<=R sqrt(p) of the fixed-lambda KL-regularized logistic policy objective estimated by known-propensity IPW, exact same-coordinate entropy-balanced IPW, and oracle DR. Derive their deterministic population-regret limits through a finite fixed-point/resolvent system; characterize the exact pooled-target balance-feasibility threshold and the positive/zero/negative HIR-dividend cells, including radius saturation; give plug-in phase inference away from boundaries. Consumer: high-dimensional targeting reanalyses of Ashraf-Karlan-Yin's commitment-savings trial. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The beta=theta/sqrt(p) reduction makes regret a strictly increasing function of the fitted norm, while row-sign symmetrization makes the entire true-IPW optimization law independent of gamma. A deformed-orthant calculation gives the pooled-target exact-balance threshold kappa_bal approximately 0.3043687064, rather than the naive Wendel value. Fixed-dimensional score variances are 1/8 for true IPW, 1/16 for entropy balance, and E[m(1-m)]/4 for oracle DR, so balance yields only a partial efficient-score projection. Valid finite fits show entropy-balance improvement at kappa 0.05 and 0.15 but reversal at 0.27; small policy radii create equal-regret saturation cells. Current primary and internal checks found no joint-regret collision. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove a joint deterministic equivalent with globally unique selected norms for the same-sample entropy tilts and nonconcave KL-policy optimizer, retaining tilt-policy overlaps and Jacobian response terms. EARLY KILL TEST: At gamma=1 and kappa=1/8, prove concentration of the exact same-sample entropy-balanced quadratic identity and recover its small-kappa coefficient; pivot if coherent leverage terms prevent finite closure. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/stat_hir_policy_dimension_phase.md.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The nearest HIR policy result is local and fixed-dimensional, where the objective Hessian has a classical limit and propensity estimation acts through a population score projection. With p/n bounded away from zero, the entropy tilt and policy optimizer reuse the same Gaussian rows, producing order-one tilt-policy overlaps and Jacobian-response terms. Existing proportional logistic and CGMT analyses cover a single convex or separable estimator, not a coupled exponential tilt followed by a potentially nonconcave policy optimization. The archived CausalSmith angle likewise contains only the fixed-dimensional projection comparison.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite fixed-point or resolvent system with a global-selection and uniqueness characterization for the tilt and policy norms, explicit deterministic limits for all three population regrets, and inequalities partitioning (kappa, lambda, R, gamma) into positive, zero, negative, and radius-saturated HIR-dividend cells.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Fixed-dimensional entropy-balancing existence treats the target moment as asymptotically deterministic and interior under overlap. Here the pooled target shares every Gaussian row with both arm-specific convex hulls, destroying the independence and central symmetry behind a naive Wendel calculation. The web literature documents high-dimensional infeasibility but does not locate this pooled-target threshold, while the prior CausalSmith constructions concern deterministic finite exact-balance programs or a different allocation threshold.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Classical HIR and calibration-efficiency arguments use an asymptotically rich score span while each fitted approximation is low-dimensional relative to n. Exact same-coordinate balance with p/n positive instead projects through a random design reused by the policy optimization, leaving order-one diagonal leverage, cross-row response, and tilt-Jacobian terms. The failed fold-spectrum proposal also records that an abstract splitting argument is inadequate without a concrete learner and checked covariance identity. Consequently, fixed-dimensional score variances alone cannot determine whether entropy balance realizes the full efficient projection.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An operator or resolvent formula for the same-sample and cross-fitted entropy-balanced policy scores, a rigorous expansion Regret_EB(kappa)-Regret_DR(kappa)=c1*kappa+o(kappa), and an if-and-only-if span condition under which the leverage correction and residual projection vanish.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing approximate-balance theory selects tolerances to control ATE bias, weight dispersion, or oracle inequalities. Here imbalance alters both the policy pseudo-outcome and the selected policy norm, while the regularized tilt and policy optimizer remain dependent through their shared proportional design. The regret-optimal tolerance may therefore jump at feasibility or radius-saturation boundaries. Targeted searches retrieved weighting and policy-learning results separately, but no deterministic tolerance-by-regret phase diagram.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Available universality arguments concern a single convex regularized estimator whose design can be replaced while controlling optimizer structure. The balance-policy pipeline contains an endogenous pooled target, two arm-specific exponential tilts, and a possibly nonconcave downstream maximizer, so replacing one row perturbs every weight and the selected policy simultaneously. Unequal randomization, anisotropic covariance, and arm-specific effects also defeat the benchmark row-sign symmetry. Elliptical-design results show that even existence boundaries may acquire new geometry, while the banked policy-regret work remains fixed-complexity.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either a universality result expressing all three regret limits and the feasibility boundary through stated covariance-spectrum and signal-overlap quantities, or an explicit elliptical or nonzero-CATE counterexample with a corrected fixed-point system and a rigorously different HIR-dividend sign cell.

literature_map:
Fang, Ridder, and Xie (2026, arXiv:2512.19230) is the nearest anchor: it studies KL-regularized randomized assignment, proves a fixed-dimensional policy-learning HIR effect, applies it to commitment savings, and leaves growing rule classes open.
Hirano, Imbens, and Ridder (2003, Econometrica) establish the estimated-versus-known propensity efficiency phenomenon through score projection and overidentifying restrictions.
Hainmueller (2012), Zhao and Percival (2017), and Chan, Yam, and Zhang (2016) connect entropy or calibration balance to dual propensity fitting, robustness, and fixed-dimensional efficiency.
The balance literature contains a sharp tension: fixed-dimensional overlap supports convex-hull feasibility, while Athey, Imbens, and Wager (2018) and Dai and Yan (2024) note that exact balance can fail in high dimension.
Wang and Zubizarreta (2020, Biometrika) develop approximately balancing minimal weights, providing a natural continuation beyond exact-balance feasibility.
Sur and Candès (2019, PNAS) show that proportional logistic fits have nonclassical bias and variance described by scalar state equations and offer feasible corrections.
Candès and Sur (2020, Annals of Statistics) prove a sharp Gaussian logistic-MLE existence transition, a close geometric analogue of the pooled-target balance event.
Zhao, Sur, and Candès (2022, Bernoulli) extend proportional logistic coordinate laws to arbitrary covariance; Tang and Ye (2020, EJS) show elliptical designs can alter existence-phase geometry.
Thrampoulidis, Abbasi, and Hassibi (2018, IEEE TIT) provide a CGMT and Moreau-envelope template for deterministic equivalents of convex Gaussian M-estimators.
Han and Shen (2023, arXiv:2206.07936) supply a universality route for regularized regression but also show that general isotropic designs need not be universal.
Kitagawa and Tetenov (2018), Athey and Wager (2021), and Luedtke and Chambaz (2020) provide regret, orthogonal-score, and policy-ERM foundations, but not proportional deterministic regret limits for this coupled fit.
Wager, Du, Taylor, and Tibshirani (2016) and Lu, Yang, and Wang (2025, arXiv:2309.02073) analyze randomized-trial adjustment with many covariates, including proportional-dimensional debiased linear adjustment.
Ashraf, Karlan, and Yin (2006, QJE, DOI:10.1162/qjec.2006.121.2.635) supply the application substrate: a randomized commitment-savings experiment with take-up and savings heterogeneity relevant to targeting.
The searched literatures meet at the topic boundary but do not jointly treat same-sample entropy tilts, proportional logistic policy optimization, KL regret, exact feasibility, and phase-label inference.
